title: Penalties by kind of violation and kind of respondent
question: Which kinds of violation and which kinds of respondent draw the Ethics Commission's penalties, how large are they, how long do they take, and who has been penalised more than once?
finding: Campaign cases are 108 of the 164 penalties and $666,418 of the $1.0 million. 23 penalties ($159,200) fell on appointed board and commission members, 5 on elected officials in ethics cases and 11 on lobbyists. 14 respondent names appear in two or more cases, among them Stacy Owens (6 cases, 2020/2021), Norman Yee (3 cases, 2013/2021), Jane Kim (3 cases, 2015/2019), Wendy Aragon (2 cases, 2014/2015).
how: The same records, years and sums as the previous screen. Kind of violation is read from the Commission's own category and the code sections it lists (a case with several violations is placed under the first that matches, in the order gifts, conflicts, contracting, advocacy, disclosure). Kind of respondent for ethics cases is read from the first respondent's positions on Form 700 cover pages, matched on the full name (an elected office first, then a department head or deputy, then a board or commission seat); campaign cases are grouped as committees and candidates because the file does not say whether the candidate held office. A repeat respondent is a name that appears in the respondents of two or more case numbers.
limits: Counts follow what the Commission chose and was able to pursue, not how often each rule is broken; campaign filings are public and easy to audit, which is one reason they dominate. A committee and its treasurer are both respondents in one case, and a professional treasurer who serves many campaigns can appear in several cases for clients' errors. A respondent matched to a Form 700 by name may be a different person of the same name, and one who left City service before electronic filing has no position on file. Medians over a handful of cases mean little.
